description: Propensity convergence sweep (500/1000/2000/5000/20000 GD iterations vs Newton/IRLS reference), support diagnostics under each fit, out-of-band patient attribution, and the pre-7.5 six-covariate comparison. Plan items 2-4.
findings: The shipped 500-iteration fit is unconverged in every fold (grad norm 6.7e-3 to 1.0e-2; coefficients shrunk, e.g. fold 0 hemophilia 0.22 vs optimum 1.09). IRLS converges cleanly (cond(H) 106-208, no separation, prior_opportunistic_infection coefficient about -1.3, finite).

The out-of-band patient is NOT an under-fitting artifact: The out-of-band patient (arm 0, Karnofsky z = -4.40, prior ART duration z = +2.94) is above 0.90 under every budget and under IRLS (0.9305 -> 0.9327). It stays inside the [0.05, 0.95] sensitivity band.

It is caused by the task 7.5 widening: under the old 6-covariate model the same patient sits at 0.876 (500) / 0.869 (converged). The new prior_art_duration term (+0.58 to +0.78 logit) and homosexual_activity push it over 0.90; Karnofsky (+1.56) is the dominant driver in both models.
Converging makes overlap slightly worse, not better: ESS 184.74/144.40 -> 179.55/138.47 (14 columns), 187.23/161.00 -> 185.28/157.75 (6 columns). Both stay well above the 100 floor.
The earlier clean 6-covariate result (ESS 187.23/161.00, extreme 0) was also from an unconverged fit, but its extreme_weight_count conclusion holds when converged.
Plain GD needs about 21k-35k iterations to reach grad norm 1e-6 (about 40-70x the shipped budget); Newton/IRLS converges in a handful of iterations. No ridge is needed.
